findings.title: Wrong thought flagged when nested in-progress
findings.problem: flagThoughtError (new in this diff) only searches top-level historyItem.thoughts for an in-progress entry via [...thoughts].reverse().find(t => t.in_progress); it never recurses into thought.children, even though Thought.children is a live nesting mechanism (a child thought is pushed onto existingParentThought.children at chatGeneration.ts:1614-1615, and Thought.children is itself typed as Thought[] with its own in_progress field, per src/types/entity/conversation.ts:106-116).
findings.impact: When a terminal chunk reports an error and the actual in-progress thought is nested under a parent's children (not a top-level entry), the top-level find() returns nothing and the code falls back to thoughts[thoughts.length - 1]: an unrelated, already-finished top-level thought is marked errored instead of the real in-progress one, and the genuinely failing nested thought is left unflagged. This is a correctness regression in code newly introduced by FE2/AC8 (the whole flagThoughtError/surfaceTerminalChunkError pair did not exist before this diff, confirmed via git diff HEAD~2).
findings.recommendation: Recurse into thought.children when searching for the in-progress thought, mirroring the recursive pattern already used by markThoughtDone (chatGeneration.ts:242-245) and _findThought, so a nested in-progress thought is located before falling back to the last top-level thought.
